_doctrine: THE MEMBERSHIP ANCHOR. A byte-faithful transcription of the sealed authority graphic, created 2026-07-15 to give essentials-canon.json's MEMBERSHIP an anchor outside our own app. Until this file existed, the canon's membership + tier partition + mineral symbols traced to `dashboard/components/workspace-coverage-v3.2-PROPOSAL.html` -- a UI DESIGN MOCKUP -- via views/coverage.ts -> coverage-layout-data.json -> the canon bootstrap on 2026-06-24 (three days after the mockup). The canon's own `provenance` field says so in plain text. The tell: the canon's rare_trace order is alphabetical BY ATOMIC SYMBOL (Ag, Al, As, Au, Ba, Be), which is how a list is lifted off a rendered table, not authored from a source. This file breaks that loop: the JPG is sealed by graphics_integrity, this transcription is bound to the JPG's exact bytes via source.file_sha256, and essentials_canon_matches_graphic gates the canon against this. WHAT IS *NOT* PROVEN: that this transcription is an accurate READING of the image. No machine can check that. It is human-verifiable -- open the JPG and compare -- and that is the honest limit (R7). It is still strictly better than the mockup: a wrong transcription is visible to any human who looks, whereas the mockup's provenance was invisible for three weeks under a green board.

source.authority: Luneth's ruling: this graphic is THE 90/91 source (memory: essentials-authority-graphic). The graphics manifest admits it as Tier-1 'treated as direct Wallach info'.
source.transcribed_by: Claude, reading the sealed image directly. VERIFY BY EYE against the JPG — that is the only check that exists for this step.

_reading_notes.layout: The 60 minerals are printed as ONE FLAT LIST in three columns of 20, alphabetical A→Z across columns. THE GRAPHIC HAS NO TIERS. It does not group minerals into foundational / major / trace / rare anything. This is independent corroboration of the 2026-07-15 finding that the app's FOUNDATIONAL(11) / MAJOR TRACE(14) / RARE TRACE(35) partition is an editorial invention: Wallach names three categories once (immortality.txt:3760-3766 — 'Major minerals / Trace minerals / Rare earths') and never assigns elements to them, and his own authority graphic lists them flat.
_reading_notes.vitamin_count: 17 lines are printed, but the graphic's own footnote reads '* D2 and D3 considered a single vitamin (Vitamin D).' — so the count is 16, exactly as the heading says.
_reading_notes.essential_count: 60 + 16 + 12 + 3 = 91 items; omega-9 is footnoted '* Becomes essential if deficient in linoleic acid.' → 90 essential. Matches the heading '90' and Wallach's own books (dddl-third-edition-2011.txt:4196, 'consuming all 90 essential nutrients in optimal amounts each day').
_reading_notes.graphic_typos: The graphic itself misprints four amino acids: 'Arqinine' (Arginine), 'Hisladine' (Histidine), 'Tourine' (Taurine), 'Tyrasine' (Tyrosine). Transcribed AS PRINTED in `as_printed`, mapped to the correct slug in `canon_slug`. Do not 'fix' the as_printed values — they are what the image says.
_reading_notes.fatty_acid_divergence: The graphic labels Omega 3 as '(Linoleic)' and Omega 6 as '(Linolenic)' — which is SWAPPED relative to standard biochemistry (omega-3 = alpha-linolenic/ALA; omega-6 = linoleic/LA) — and Omega 9 as '(Arachidonic)' where the canon says Oleic. The canon deliberately diverges; see chronicle/contradictions/2026-07-08-omega9-arachidonic-correction.md. THIS FILE ANCHORS MEMBERSHIP (which 91 substances), NOT the parenthetical sub-names. The gate compares membership only, and says so.
